To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) classification accuracy is an inadequate performance indicator in the presence of temporal dependence, 2) the Kappa statistic is a misleading performance indicator in the case of temporal dependence, and 3) the combined measure of classification performance, which takes into account temporal dependency, should be used in evaluation of data stream classification algorithms.

(1) the commonly accepted data classification measures, such classification accuracy and K kappa, are not suitable for evaluation of classifiers in the stream setting, and they should not be the only measures used for classifier evaluation; (2) the proposed combined measure is the most suitable for classifier evaluation in the stream setting; (3) classification accuracy is a misleading performance measure for evaluating change detectors in the stream setting.
